jobs.label: Quantity up

concepts.name: The marker posts
concepts.note: The fifth you just crossed, shown as five posts on one line with the date each one fell. Quantity up with a target has natural chapters at every fifth, and dating them turns a progress bar into a history: Mar 3, Jun 1, today. The line says 216 days made these 60, then 40 still open, so the distance closed and the distance left both get stated. One accent: the post that just landed. Passed posts now step taller toward today, still uncolored (2026-08-10).

concepts.name: Four figures
concepts.note: No target on this goal, so the win is that the number grew a digit. The last five months sit as a small ledger and the lit rule is the thousand line, with August above it for the first time. Order of magnitude works when a percentage cannot exist, and the old best (840) is right there for scale. The M sits quiet at the foot of the deposit.

concepts.name: The days you will not need
concepts.note: A deadline goal reached early, where the reward is the time handed back. The run from Feb 1 to Dec 31 is drawn once, and the lit tail is the 53 days you set aside and never needed. Beating a date is worth more than hitting a number, and this is the only way to show it without a countdown. One accent: the unused stretch.

concepts.name: The record board
concepts.note: No target at all, so the only thing to beat is the last time you were best. The new week takes the top seat and pushes the old records down, and the caption says the one it beat stood 22 weeks, which is what makes it mean something. A personal record rewards the fact instead of a fraction, so a goal with no end still gets a real moment.

remaining: note, non-blocking: qu-2 (78px) and qu-5 (88px) heroes sit between the 68px and 104px tokens. Kept deliberately, the strings $1,000 and 1,412 overflow the 330px content width at 104px, and off-scale hero sizes already exist elsewhere in the set (ms-3, ms-4 at 56px).

jobs.label: Quantity down

concepts.name: The slider down
concepts.note: REBUILT 2026-08-10 (Malik: horizontal, numbers on a slider showing where they are and where they are going). One line: the start weight named on the left, the goal named on the right, the real fifths as small weights above the line, and the accent post carrying today's number. The travelled stretch of the line is brighter. Positions are plain percentages of start-to-goal, so any pair of numbers lays out correctly.

concepts.name: The record book
concepts.note: REBUILT AGAIN 2026-08-10 (Malik: screen time, his audience's real fight). One concrete case: "less time on my phone", no hard target, the week's daily average logged. The record book is their own lowest weeks; the only thing to beat is themselves.

concepts.name: The number you carry
concepts.note: The scale reading falls from 214 to 199 in front of you with a soft breath of your colour behind it. For weight and debt the number people hold in their head is the current one, not the amount lost, so the current one is the hero and beat 2 pays the receipt: 96 days, and the last time you were under 200 was 2019. His line added verbatim: "You said you wanted to be under 200."

concepts.name: The fall, drawn
concepts.note: A 34,000 loan with 29,900 still open, so the win is the balance dropping and a line is literally drawn from the old figure down to the new one. The closed and open amounts sit together underneath, because on a long road hiding the remainder is what makes a screen feel fake.

concepts.name: The line you got under
concepts.note: A threshold goal, so the accent is the 1h line and the week's average sits under it. Beat 2 turns the drop into something you can feel, 15 hours of your week handed back, which is the only reward a falling number can really offer.

remaining: non-blocking, no rule broken: qd-1's deposit line 'On this day, you reached 8 lbs down of 20.' is slightly clumsy grammar next to the KIT's example shape ('On this day, you lost 4 lbs.'). It is a plain, adjective-free, exclamation-free log sentence, so it is compliant. Left alone rather than rewriting the concept's copy.

jobs.label: Frequency

concepts.name: Four of four
concepts.note: The week you asked for, closed. Beat one is just 4 of 4, beat two is the seven day columns with Saturday lit as the run that closed it, beat three is the log line. It suits frequency because the unit of truth here is the week, not the day, and the chart shows the rest days as normal rather than as gaps.

concepts.name: Six weeks running
concepts.note: Six weeks of writing stacked as a small calendar block, with one accent line down the left holding them together as a single run. The rate is the point, so the reward is the shape of the last six weeks rather than a count of consecutive days. Nothing here can be broken by one quiet morning.

concepts.name: The fiftieth
concepts.note: Fifty runs as fifty dots, the last one lit. The number lands alone first, then the cost arrives, 101 days and 268 miles. Rep milestones are the one place frequency gets a real, rare hit, and a countable field of evidence beats any badge. This is the only screen in my five carrying the M, quiet at the foot. Label now "Total runs" (2026-08-10).

concepts.name: Twelve of fourteen
concepts.note: The tolerant one. It counts the rate across a 14 week window, so the week he was away renders as a small quiet stub instead of a break, and the copy says plainly there is nothing to make up. The accent sits on this week's bar, the return, so the reward is for showing up again and not for never missing.

concepts.name: Weeks to the start line
concepts.note: Frequency with a deadline. Nine weeks kept shown as a runway of sixteen with a tick at race day, so the deed already banked is the coloured part and the future is only a quiet marker. It states the seven weeks still open honestly, without turning them into pressure.

remaining: Judgment call, not a violation, left unchanged: fr-5's accent is a 9-segment filled rail against 7 empty segments running to a race-day marker. It is one accent moment and KIT section 11 explicitly sanctions stating distance closed alongside distance open, so it passes the contract. But it is the largest accent mass in the family (the other four are a single bar, line, dot or column) and it is the only screen that reads as a progress bar. Flagging in case Malik wants the family visually uniform.

Judgment call, not a violation, left unchanged: fr-1's .cap carries a full sentence ("Saturday closed the week.") at 12.5px on --text-lo, which brushes the dim-body-text law. Left as is because .cap is the kit's own token used identically across all 45 screens; changing it here would break cohesion with the set rather than fix a local error.

jobs.label: Maintenance

concepts.name: The ledger of days
concepts.note: Day 100 sober on a goal with no end date. Beat 2 draws the hundred days as a dense block of tick marks, four rows of twenty five, so the days read as a ledger already written rather than a streak that could snap. The closing line says it out loud: no end date, and the hundred days are in the record now. Fits maintenance because the only honest number a held line has is time, and time already spent cannot be withdrawn.

concepts.name: Held to the date
concepts.note: The hold-until-deadline completion, a no-buy year that reaches its own end date. A rail runs from the start date to the date they picked and fills all the way across, and the end node lands. This is the one maintenance case where the goal actually finishes, so beat 3 says the year held and the goal is complete, then adds that there is nothing left to hold. No fear of tomorrow because there is no tomorrow on this one.

concepts.name: The hard ones
concepts.note: Day 30 off nicotine pouches, told through the days that nearly went. Thirty bars sit at one height, then the nine days they logged as hard stand up in the accent. It acknowledges the cost without any drama, just a count. The close is the whole point for this type: the nine hard days are spent and counted, they do not come back around. Data note: the hard days are REAL, they come from the daily check-in (mood 1-2 of 5, already in state.checkins). The beat only renders when check-ins exist; without them it swaps to a plain day-count receipt. Nothing invented. SCOPE (Malik 2026-08-10): the "today felt hard" log is OFFERED ONLY on maintenance/quit-a-habit goals, never forced on everyone; mt-3 renders only when hard days were actually logged.

concepts.name: The first seven
concepts.note: The smallest maintenance marker taken seriously. A soft accent wash behind the number 7, then seven plain strokes for seven nights the phone stayed out of the bedroom. Week one is where people quit because nothing has changed yet, so the deposit line answers that directly: nothing looks different yet, the count does. Restraint is the design, a big ceremony on day 7 would be a lie.

concepts.name: The trail of markers
concepts.note: One year sober, shown as the fourth marker on a trail: 7, 30, 100, and today, with only today in the accent. It reframes a long hold as a set of separate deposits instead of one tall thing that can fall, since every earlier marker stays passed no matter what happens next. The close states it plainly, whatever tomorrow does, these 365 days already happened.

remaining: Not visually verified in a browser: the tab cap was full (8 tabs held by sibling agents in this session) and tabs_create/preview_start both refused, so I could not screenshot the 390x760 frames across the six accents. Both edits are low layout risk (a 2px tick colour swap, and one note line that grows from ~2 to ~3 wrapped lines at 26ch inside a sparse beat 3), but neither has been looked at. Worth a glance when the maintenance page is next built.

mt-5.html copy/CSS mismatch, judgment call, NOT a contract violation so left alone: the file comment says "the three markers already banked behind it" while beat 2 reads "Four markers behind you now" over a 7/30/100/365 trail where 365 is the current stop. The on-screen copy is defensible (365 is banked too); only the developer comment is off.

jobs.label: Open

concepts.name: Two entries, 90 days apart
concepts.note: Their day one journal lands alone, then this week's entry appears under it with the accent rule beside it. Their words are the whole screen, awkward spelling and the tuesday he still snapped included. Open goals have nothing to count, so the only honest proof is that the person writing today is not the person who wrote in March. CADENCE (Malik 2026-08-10): fires first at day 30, then on the ladder, never a 90-day wait.

concepts.name: 180 days, the sentence intact
concepts.note: The day count lands first, then what they wrote on February 8, word for word. Time plus their own sentence, nothing added. The accent is a small tick under the number instead of the number itself, so it never reads as a score on a goal that cannot be scored.

concepts.name: Day 30, the goal and the why
concepts.note: ENRICHED 2026-08-10 (was goal + why alone, "meh"). The why quote stays the heart; the land beat now carries real receipts, days carried and entries written, before the deposit line.

concepts.name: A year, still open
concepts.note: Their sentence with a thin accent line running off the bottom of the screen, then 365 and the plain fact that this one has no finish. Open goals never complete, and pretending otherwise would be a lie, so the deposit says still open and leaves it there. Malik loves it but a year must not be the first sighting; earlier rungs come from the same day ladder.

remaining: non-blocking, not a rule violation: op-1.html line 13 uses margin-bottom:152px to pin the first entry across beats 1 and 2, but the late block measures ~165px, so the entry settles up about 13px on the beat change. Imperceptible under the cross-fade; left alone rather than guess a new magic number.

non-blocking, not a rule violation: op-1.html's beat-3 deposit ('Day 90. Your first entry and today's are kept together.') describes what is filed rather than what the user did, making it the softest of the five deposits. It still satisfies the plain-log-line rule, so rewriting it would have been a concept change rather than enforcement.

context for the parent, not an op-* defect: a headless render of op-5 showed the counter stuck at 0. This is the shared countUp in _kit.js stalling under Chrome's virtual-time budget, not a fragment bug. It counted correctly at other budgets and in op-2.

jobs.label: The four refinements

concepts.name: The Gap
concepts.note: The goal is a distance, so the ceremony is that distance closing. The ground already covered goes solid in their colour, what is left stays a dotted line, and a faint tick marks where they stood at the last marker so the span they just closed is visible. The remaining number is never hidden, it sits at the same weight as the closed one and it is still there on the final beat. This is the honest version of a progress bar and the one that fits any quantity goal with a target.

concepts.name: The Fall
concepts.note: For a losing or paying-off goal, the number people carry in their head is what is left, so that is the number that drops. It falls with weight, presses into the line under it, and the line takes the impact and lights. Beat two turns the whole descent into a ledger: every floor already passed and the day it happened, which says the drop was work and not luck. Suits quantity down, where a percentage would feel like the app grading them.

concepts.name: The Record
concepts.note: Twelve weeks of days, and the ones they showed up light in the order they actually happened. The empty squares stay in, because a four times a week goal has gaps and hiding them would make it a trophy instead of evidence. Today is the only square in their colour, the last one to land. Built from the consistency data the app already keeps, which is why it fits frequency goals better than any counter.

remaining: rf-fall.html line 45: .fl__day uses rgba(var(--ink),.52), a custom alpha instead of a token. Not a dim-text violation (brighter than --text-lo, and it is a 12.5px label, not a sentence), and normalizing it to --text-mid would erase the contrast that marks the current row. Left as-is, flagged only.

Verification caveat: the browser pane was at its tab cap (parallel agents holding all 9 tabs), so all 12 beats were rendered via headless Chrome at end state in cyan, amber and rose rather than driven live. Beat timing was checked by reading delay stacks against the kit's 1900/2300ms dwells (longest chain, rf-gap beat 2 settling at 1.96s, fits its window).

concepts.name: The Grand Finale
concepts.note: Malik's pick, fused: the M fades in with colour, the Crown's rings collapse into it, "guess what...", then a tap floats the M up and detonates into the Fireworks with the goal line centred. Swipe the stats between a slowly turning 3D sphere of every move and the numbers.
